subject: Clarify downtime calculation for probe-fanout incident overlapping maintenance
messages:
From: Emily Turner <emily.turner@corridornet.com>
To: rafael.mendes@redwood.com, ben.carter@redwood.com
Cc: noc@corridornet.com
Date: Thu, 24 Jun 2027 17:22:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Clarify downtime calculation for probe-fanout incident overlapping maintenance

Hi Rafael / Ben,

We flagged a customer-impacting window yesterday (2027-06-24 15:04–15:22 UTC) and CorridorNet’s synthetic monitoring shows a ~2.3% availability hit for our API paths during that interval. Your uptime report (attached) lists the majority of the minutes under a Redwood maintenance exception, which is puzzling because our probes continued to reach multiple POPs and only a subset showed errors.

Two items we need from you to reconcile the calc ASAP:
- Raw probe-level timestamps from Redwood’s edge for 15:00–15:30 UTC (all POPs involved).
- Explanation of how maintenance windows are applied when only specific egress paths are affected — we think there may be probe fanout duplication where our single probe hits multiple Redwood collectors and the minutes are being double-counted.

This is important for our billing team — please treat as high priority. I’ve attached our monitoring extract (uptime_report_CorridorNet.csv).

Thanks,
Emily
Emily Turner
SRE Lead, CorridorNet
emily.turner@corridornet.com
+1 415 555 0198
From: Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwood.com>
To: Emily Turner <emily.turner@corridornet.com>
Cc: ben.carter@redwood.com, marissa.cole@redwood.com
Date: Thu, 24 Jun 2027 18:08:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Clarify downtime calculation for probe-fanout incident overlapping maintenance

Hi Emily — thanks for the heads up and the CSV. I’ve opened an internal triage and asked our edge team to pull the collector logs for 15:00–15:30 UTC across the POPs you hit. We’ll also verify the maintenance tag boundaries and whether the probe identifiers you mentioned caused duplicate minute attribution.

Short timeline: we had a pre-announced maintenance window from 15:06–15:13 UTC for a control-plane rollout in a subset of east coast POPs (notice attached: maintenance_window_notice.pdf). Preliminary look suggests two things could be happening simultaneously: (1) our maintenance affected only the control-plane signaling to some collectors for ~7 minutes and (2) we saw a brief partial-degradation event on an upstream provider’s uplink that caused packet loss in a subset of collectors from 15:09–15:18 UTC.

I’ll loop in Marcus (edge infra) with logs and get you an initial breakdown within 24 hours. If you need an interim confirmation for billing, tell your team we’ve acknowledged the discrepancy and are treating it as an investigatory SLA exception.

Best,
Rafael Mendes
Account Exec, Redwood Inference
rafael.mendes@redwood.com

From: Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 24 Jun 2027 18:08:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Clarify downtime calculation for probe-fanout incident overlapping maintenance
Team — Emily from CorridorNet attached their probe dump. They’re seeing availability delta and suspect our maintenance window tagging + probe fanout is producing double-counting in their aggregated minutes. Please pull collector logs for 2027-06-24 15:00–15:30 UTC across these POPs: iad1, atl1, ord1, and check per-probe identifiers so we can map their probes to collector events.
Ben
From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
To: ben.carter@redwood.com, rafael.mendes@redwood.com
Cc: marissa.cole@redwood.com
Date: Fri, 25 Jun 2027 13:45:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Fwd: Clarify downtime calculation for probe-fanout incident overlapping maintenance

Quick summary from the edge analysis (attachments: redwood_probe_logs_0624.gz, uptime_calc_breakdown.csv):
- We correlated CorridorNet probe IDs with collector receipts. Their single probe fanouts hit 3 collectors in some cases (iad1 -> iad1-prim, iad1-sec, ord1-prim). We dedup at request-id when computing per-customer minutes, but CorridorNet’s downstream aggregation treats each collector receipt as an independent failure sample which can inflate their external view.
- Maintenance window: control-plane rollout was limited to iad1 control-plane agents between 15:06:00–15:13:00 UTC. Data-plane continued serving; collectors kept accepting telemetry. We tag minutes fully as ‘maintenance’ when any control-plane action could affect signaling for that minute — this is conservative and aligns with the contract language, but it risks masking partial-degradation elsewhere.
- Upstream provider issue: between 15:09:30–15:18:10 UTC we see increased 5xx and TCP retransmits on the ord1 uplink impacting ~12% of connections; this is independent of our rollout and correlates with the customer-visible errors in their CSV.
Recommendation for credit calc: prorate the overlap. Minutes 15:06–15:09 should be maintenance-covered (full exclusion). Minutes 15:09–15:18 should be split: part attributable to a third-party uplink degradation (exclude per-contract) and part attributable to partial loss where customer probes were duplicated across collectors (we should avoid double-counting when evaluating the customer view). I propose a pragmatic credit of 40% of the billed minutes in 15:09–15:18 as an agreement to close quickly.

I’ll attach the minute-by-minute table and the per-probe mapping so CorridorNet can see the dedupe keys.
Marcus
Principal SRE, Redwood Inference
From: Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwood.com>
To: Emily Turner <emily.turner@corridornet.com>
Cc: ben.carter@redwood.com, marissa.cole@redwood.com, marcus.lin@redwood.com
Date: Sat, 26 Jun 2027 11:30:00 +0000
Subject: Proposed reconciliation and next steps — CorridorNet incident 2027-06-24
Hi Emily — thanks for patience while we investigated. Summary and proposed next steps below.

What we found:
- Maintenance window (15:06–15:13 UTC) was limited to control-plane agents in iad1; data-plane collectors remained active.
- Between 15:09:30–15:18:10 UTC an upstream provider had packet loss affecting ord1, producing genuine 5xx spikes for a subset of customer traffic.
- CorridorNet probes sometimes fan out to multiple collectors; if they aggregate raw receipts without dedupe by request-id that can inflate error counts. Our internal SLA tally deduplicates by request-id.

Proposed reconciliation:
- Treat 15:06–15:09 as Redwood maintenance exception (no credit).
- For 15:09–15:18, propose a 40% credit against billed minutes for that window. Rationale: split responsibility between upstream provider and the overlap in probe-fanout semantics; avoids prolonged disputes and aligns with our precedent for partial-degradation proration.
- Deliverables: minute-by-minute CSV and sample dedupe keys (attached), plus raw collector receipts (redwood_probe_logs_0624.gz).

Request from you:
1) Confirm you accept the 40% reconciliation and we’ll submit the SLA credit.
2) If you want us to recompute their billing using CorridorNet’s aggregation rules instead of ours, confirm and we’ll run that as an add-on analysis (may take 48h).
3) Proposed postmortem call: Mon 2027-06-28 15:00 UTC — please confirm attendees.

If accepted we will open a billing adjustment and issue a credit memoire referencing DEAL-8702.

Best regards,
Rafael Mendes
Account Exec, Redwood Inference
rafael.mendes@redwood.com
From: Emily Turner <emily.turner@corridornet.com>
To: Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwood.com>
Cc: noc@corridornet.com
Date: Sun, 27 Jun 2027 12:03:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Proposed reconciliation and next steps — CorridorNet incident 2027-06-24

Rafael — thanks for the clear breakdown and for providing the logs. We accept the 40% credit for 15:09–15:18 as a pragmatic resolution. Please proceed with the billing adjustment and send the formal credit calculation (line items) so our finance team can process. We’ll join the postmortem on Mon 2027-06-28 15:00 UTC — attendees: Emily Turner, Sanjay Rao (SRE), Priya Mehta (Billing).

Also, can you upload the minute-by-minute table and the dedupe mapping to the HubSpot record with id 8702 and attach the DocuSign credit memo? Our procurement needs DocuSign to complete the refund.

Regards,
Emily
SRE Lead, CorridorNet
